category.label: Magnesium
category.comparisonNote: Cost comparisons use explicitly labelled elemental magnesium. Glycinate, citrate and other compound masses are stored separately and are not substituted for elemental content.

guide.title: Magnesium: elemental amounts before salt names
guide.summary: Glycinate, citrate and oxide describe compounds. Their full mass must not be mistaken for elemental magnesium.
guide.evidence: Magnesium is an essential nutrient; the evidence and relevance of supplementation depend on the indication and baseline nutritional status.
guide.limitations: Absorption differences between forms do not, by themselves, establish superiority for sleep or athletic recovery. Broad wellness claims need outcome-specific trials.
guide.catalogReading: Compare explicitly labelled elemental magnesium per serving. The site keeps compound mass separate and withholds active-content cost when elemental amounts or serving size are unclear.
guide.safety: Supplemental magnesium can cause diarrhoea and interact with some medicines. Kidney impairment changes safety considerations; seek individual advice.
guide.author: Supplement Research editorial synthesis
bodySteps: A magnesium compound must release magnesium that can be absorbed from the intestine.
Absorbed magnesium supports enzyme activity, energy metabolism, and normal nerve and muscle function.
The kidneys help regulate magnesium balance by adjusting excretion.
guide.treatment: Replacement treats magnesium deficiency when indicated. Some magnesium medicines act as laxatives or antacids; this does not make every supplement a treatment for constipation, insomnia or cramps.
guide.whoMayBenefit: People with a diagnosed deficiency or an assessed intake or absorption problem, with attention to kidney function and medicines.
guide.routineUse: No universal need for magnesium tablets if intake is adequate. Symptoms such as cramps alone do not establish deficiency.

whoCanConsider: Adults with an assessed magnesium shortfall that food changes cannot readily address.
People with diagnosed deficiency or ongoing losses following a clinician's plan.
whoShouldReview: Impaired kidney function raises the risk from excess supplemental magnesium.
Certain antibiotics, oral bisphosphonates, diuretics or long-term acid-suppressing medicines require review.
buyingGuide.foodSummary: Magnesium is available across common plant foods; dietary variety can address many intake gaps.

dos.title: Look for elemental magnesium
dos.detail: Compare its verified amount per serving, rather than the larger mass of a magnesium salt.

dos.title: Review food and medicines
dos.detail: Check the reason for supplementation, existing intake, tolerability and relevant medicine or kidney-health concerns.

donts.title: Don't infer missing active content
donts.detail: An unclear elemental amount or serving size prevents a reliable active-content cost comparison.

donts.title: Don't assume a universal sleep benefit
donts.detail: A salt name or an adequate mineral intake does not establish that adding magnesium will improve everyone's sleep.

intakeGuide.summary: Meet the age- and sex-specific total dietary reference. A reference intake is not the same as a supplemental dose or deficiency-treatment regimen.

limits.notes: Includes supplements and medicines; excludes magnesium naturally in food. Kidney disease needs clinical review.

pathway.title: An absorbed mineral used by cellular enzymes
pathway.summary: Magnesium supplies an essential ion for many reactions; it is not an energy source. Kidneys adjust urinary losses to help regulate its balance.

steps.label: Compounds supply absorbable magnesium ions
steps.detail: Magnesium from foods and dissolved supplement compounds is absorbed by the intestine; the absorbed fraction varies.

steps.label: Magnesium supports cellular enzyme systems
steps.detail: Magnesium acts as a cofactor in hundreds of enzyme systems, including those involved in glycolysis and protein synthesis.

steps.label: Enzymes and ion transport support function
steps.detail: These roles contribute to energy metabolism, nerve signalling and muscle contraction.

pathway.caveat: Normal biochemical roles do not establish extra performance or sleep benefits in everyone. Kidney impairment can reduce the ability to clear excess magnesium.
